title: From the last vector to the next token
note: text = subtitles; say = spelled for the voice. Numbers from brain3d/trace.json, films/qkv_data.json and build/data/next_token_*.json (capture_next_gen.py).

blocks.text: So far: Emma's text became 100 tokens. Each token became a vector of 896 numbers. 24 blocks updated every vector, in one pass. And we keep just one: the last position's final vector.
blocks.say: So far: Emma's text became one hundred tokens. Each token became a vector of eight hundred and ninety-six numbers. Twenty-four blocks updated every vector, in one pass. And we keep just one: the last position's final vector.

blocks.text: Now: how does that vector become the next token?
blocks.say: Now: how does that vector become the next token?

blocks.text: First, a final RMSNorm. It divides all 896 numbers by their root mean square, here 1.89, then multiplies each by a learned gain. Same direction, fixed scale.
blocks.say: First, a final RMS Norm. It divides all eight hundred and ninety-six numbers by their root mean square, here one point eight nine, then multiplies each by a learned gain. Same direction, fixed scale.

blocks.text: Then, scoring. The model's table has one row per token: 151,936 rows of 896 numbers. Multiply the vector with a row, number by number, and add it up: one dot product, one score. For We, it comes to 20.84.
blocks.say: Then, scoring. The model's table has one row per token: one hundred and fifty-one thousand, nine hundred and thirty-six rows of eight hundred and ninety-six numbers. Multiply the vector with a row, number by number, and add it up: one dot product, one score. For We, it comes to twenty point eight four.

blocks.text: And this table? We have met it before. It is the embedding table from section 3. The same table that reads tokens in now scores them on the way out: tied weights.

blocks.text: That gives one score per row, called a logit. Only five pass 18. We: 20.84. As: 18.88. Manchester: 18.62.
blocks.say: That gives one score per row, called a logit. Only five pass eighteen. We: twenty point eight four. As: eighteen point eight eight. Manchester: eighteen point six two.

blocks.text: Softmax turns them into probabilities. Raise e to each logit: for We, 1.13 billion. Divide by the sum over every row: 2.0 billion. We gets 56 percent. As, 8. Manchester, 6. All together, one.
blocks.say: Softmax turns them into probabilities. Raise e to each logit: for We, one point one three billion. Divide by the sum over every row: two point oh billion. We gets fifty-six percent. As, eight. Manchester, six. All together, one.

blocks.text: Then one token is picked. Greedy takes the top one: We, every time. Sampling spins a weighted wheel. Five real spins: As. City. We. We. We. In a thousand spins, We wins 582.

blocks.text: Temperature divides the logits first. At 0.7, the gaps grow: We rises to 82 percent. At 1.2, they shrink: We falls to 41. And temperature zero is greedy.
blocks.say: Temperature divides the logits first. At zero point seven, the gaps grow: We rises to eighty-two percent. At one point two, they shrink: We falls to forty-one. And temperature zero is greedy.

blocks.text: Our run is greedy, so the choice is We. It joins the end of the text, and the whole machine runs again.
